counterfactual_missing_items: No histopathologic confirmation of non-caseating granulomatous inflammation is provided.

decisive_items: An infectious workup, including inflammatory markers and cultures, was strictly normal.
She had no history of tuberculosis or tuberculous contact.
Breast MRI revealed multiple oval and rounded lesions with irregular thick walls throughout the gland, extending to the skin, with peripheral enhancement.
response.rationale: C1 inherits the full IGLM diagnosis from R5 plus the right-side anatomy, while R5 is nearly the same but lacks the right-breast completion. R2 is the same broad granulomatous family but omits lobular/idiopathic specificity and laterality; R1 uses shared nipple/fistula findings but cannot account convincingly for the multifocal intra-glandular MRI pattern and strictly non-infectious, antibiotic-refractory course.

rejected.why: Granulomatous mastitis is etiologically correct but is a less specific diagnostic frame that is subsumed by R5/C1 and adds no independent supporting features.

Nipple retraction and fistula are periductal mastitis-compatible, but the documented MRI pattern, the diffusely located enhancing lesions, the negative infectious work-up, and failure to respond to fluoroquinolone are all more compatible with granulomatous lobular mastitis than periductal duct-centered mastitis.
